paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:8, Rabbi Yehudah, son of Rabbi Bun, says, “and not retroactively.” At the end of Ketubot 5:6, Rabbi Yudah, son of Rabbi Bun, says that a woman does not usually sit idle, etc. Hyman suggests both places may need to read Rabbi Yose, son of Rabbi Bun. See Rabbi Yehudah ben Buni.

notes.text: The proposed Yose reading is Hyman’s conjecture; the cited forms Yehudah/Yudah son of Bun are not silently replaced.

The consulted Rosh Hashanah 1:8 reads Yose beRabbi Bun, whereas Ketubot 5:6 reads Yudah beRabbi Bun. Hyman reports Yehudah/Yudah in both and proposes Yose; these occurrence-specific forms are not silently harmonized.
